title: Algorithms, Data Structures, and Algorithm Design Foundations

sources.notes: MIT OCW course identity for mathematical modeling of computational problems, common algorithms, algorithmic paradigms, data structures, performance measures, analysis techniques, and the relationship between algorithms and programming.

Lecture-note and recitation index for data structures, sorting, hashing, binary trees, AVL trees, heaps, BFS, DFS, weighted shortest paths, Bellman-Ford, Dijkstra, all-shortest paths, dynamic programming, subset sums, pseudopolynomial algorithms, and complexity; PDFs and videos remain child-resource boundaries.

MIT OCW intermediate algorithms identity for design and analysis of efficient algorithms, divide and conquer, randomization, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, incremental improvement, complexity, and cryptography.

Lecture-note index for interval scheduling, convex hulls, median finding, FFT, van Emde Boas trees, amortization, randomized matrix multiply, quicksort, skip lists, universal/perfect hashing, range trees, advanced dynamic programming, all-pairs shortest paths, MST, max-flow/min-cut, matching, linear programming, P/NP/NP-completeness, approximation, fixed-parameter algorithms, distributed algorithms, and cryptography; PDFs and videos remain child-resource boundaries.

MIT OCW advanced data structures identity for major results and research directions in data structures as efficient-algorithm building blocks; lecture notes, problem sets, and videos remain child-resource boundaries.

MIT OCW graduate algorithms identity for amortization, randomization, fingerprinting, word-level parallelism, bit scaling, dynamic programming, network flow, linear programming, fixed-parameter algorithms, approximation algorithms, strings, network optimization, parallel algorithms, computational geometry, online algorithms, external memory, cache, streaming, and data structures.

Jeff Erickson Algorithms identity for a free electronic algorithms textbook and lecture-note collection; page states the textbook uses CC BY 4.0 and other notes use CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, but PDFs, exercises, translations, repositories, and course archives remain boundary-checked in this tranche.

Open Data Structures identity for sequences, queues, priority queues, dictionaries, graphs, stacks, lists, hash tables, search trees, integer searching, heaps, graph representations, and B-trees; text/source license appears permissive, but book/source extraction remains deferred to a dedicated reuse review.

Algorithms, 4th Edition booksite identity for fundamentals, sorting, searching, graphs, strings, and context, with excerpts, lectures, Java code, exercises, and assignments; online content, code, exercises, videos, and textbook material remain boundary-checked.
